mcq.question: Why is `retries` a `std::optional<int>` instead of an `int` with a default of 0?

options.A: Because `int` parameters cannot have default values
options.C: So that 'not given' (use the project default) can be told apart from 'given as 0' (no retries)
options.D: Because a negative number of retries must be representable

mcq.explanation: With a plain default, the function cannot know whether the caller wanted 0 or simply said nothing. `std::nullopt` makes the absence explicit.

mcq.question: Which declaration is ill-formed in C++?

options.C: `void f(std::string name, int a = 1, int b = 2);`

mcq.explanation: Once a parameter has a default argument, every parameter after it must also have one, because arguments are matched left to right.
